prompt.es: Responde al mensaje de Kenji: explica los dos modismos en inglés sencillo.

answer.text: Hi Kenji, sorry about that. Those are idioms. “Back to square one” means we have to start again from the beginning. We made a plan, but it did not work, so we are at the start again. “Hit the nail on the head” means to say exactly the right thing. When Leo said the price was too high, he hit the nail on the head, because it was exactly the problem. In other words, the first idiom is about starting again and the second is about being exactly right. Does that make sense? I can also write without idioms next time, so please tell me if any other phrase is unclear. I will explain it in simple words. Thank you for asking!
accepted: Hi Kenji, sorry about that. Those are idioms. “Back to square one” means we have to start again from the beginning. When Leo said the price was too high, he hit the nail on the head, because it was exactly the problem. In other words, the first idiom is about starting again and the second is about being exactly right. Does that make sense? I can also write without idioms next time, so please tell me if any other phrase is unclear. I will explain it in simple words. Thank you for asking!

Hello Kenji, sorry, I used idioms. “Back to square one” means we must start again from the beginning, because our first plan did not work. “Hit the nail on the head” means to say exactly the right thing. Leo said the price was too high, and he was exactly right. In other words, the first idiom means we start again and the second means someone is correct. Is that clear? Next time I will use simple words, so please tell me if something is unclear. Thanks for asking!

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta avisa de que son modismos, explica cada uno con frases cortas, usa in other words y comprueba la comprensión.
